title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault-Injection Paired Study
abstract: We evaluate whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM-based repair workflow reduces residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair. In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired design (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) executed under shared_controlled_fault_candidate pairing semantics, we planned 40 confirmatory pairs and observed 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded per the preregistered rule). Baseline (blind repair) satisfied the verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) satisfied it in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts: n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points); two-sided exact paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Confirmatory execution used the declared model version gpt-5-mini and consumed 118 hosted-model calls (maximum planned 120). The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not present in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved for confirmatory inference; the frozen harmful-change mapping and per-episode validation traces were recorded during execution and enable deterministic independent recomputation. We present the preregistered primary result, clarify execution semantics, and state limitations and reproducibility guidance without altering the preregistered scientific record.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as aides in network operations (NetOps) for tasks such as intent-to-configuration translation and automated remediation. A practical safety architecture is generate–verify–repair (GVR): candidate configurations are checked by deterministic verifiers and, when violations are found, verifier diagnostics are fed back to a generator/repair model to produce corrected candidates. Empirical work in code and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) settings reports that inserting deterministic verifiers can increase verifier-detected pass rates while exposing new failure modes (e.g., verifier-exploitation) and incurring interaction costs [1]–[4]. Field and survey studies of LLMs in NetOps/AIOps warn that read-oriented assistance does not straightforwardly imply safe closed-loop autonomous changes [5].

Motivation and research question. Controlled paired evidence on verifier-guided repair applied to vendor command-line interface (CLI) templates with preregistered realistic fault operators is sparse. Verifier-guided repair can only affect outcomes when initial candidates trigger actionable diagnostics, so we used deterministic controlled faults that guarantee activation in a paired design that reuses the same controlled-fault candidate across arms. Our research question: Does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair when confronted with preregistered controlled faults?
sections.related_work:
Generate–verify–repair pipelines have been studied across code, IaC, and DSL settings with mixed results. Prior controlled evaluations report that deterministic verifiers interposed between generation and acceptance raise verifier-detected pass rates and that supplying verifier diagnostics to a repair generator increases the chance a corrected artifact satisfies the verifier on recheck [1], [2]. Complementary analyses document caveats: (a) single-proxy verifiers can be optimized in unintended ways (verifier-exploitation), producing pathologies under iterative refinement [3]; (b) verifier mediation imposes additional interaction and compute overhead (a "verifier tax") that depends on horizon and design choices [4]; and (c) survey and field evidence for NetOps indicates that LLMs provide useful read-oriented assistance but weaker guarantees for safe closed-loop changes without careful orchestration [5].

These prior findings motivate a controlled experiment that (i) uses deterministic verifiers, (ii) ensures intervention activation via controlled fault injection, and (iii) isolates the effect of exposing verifier diagnostics by reusing the same initial candidate across paired conditions.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered as vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where a binary success indicator requires both the deterministic vendor-CLI verifier and a simulator-based compliance agreement.

Adapter, pairing, and generation semantics. Confirmatory execution used the hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 adapter under its shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics. Under those semantics each task index received exactly one deterministically injected controlled-fault candidate which was reused unchanged across both experimental conditions; exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms. Baseline denotes blind repair (repair without exposure of verifier diagnostics) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed to the repair model. Because the same initial candidate and matched repair budget were supplied to both arms, observed differences isolate the effect of exposing diagnostics under the adapter contract rather than differences in source-generation sampling.

Model sampling and runtime parameters. The declared model used for confirmatory execution was gpt-5-mini. The archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. The adapter contract performed one sampled initial generation per pair that was reused by both arms; this study does not measure effects of independent first-pass sampling across conditions.

Controlled-challenge fault bank, scoring, and harmful-change rules. The confirmatory task bank consisted of 40 preregistered deterministic controlled-fault indices produced by deterministic_netops_fault_injector_v1. The primary success predicate required agreement between a deterministic vendor-CLI validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and a simulator-based compliance check. A frozen harmful-change mapping labeled an episode as harmful if post-repair validator traces included PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE; that mapping and the per-episode validator traces were recorded during execution and permit deterministic recomputation of the preregistered harmful-overrepair statistic by independent auditors.

Statistical analysis plan. The predefined primary test was a two-sided exact paired binary test (exact McNemar or an equivalent exact paired binomial test). We report discordant-pair counts (n10, n01), the absolute paired risk difference with a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile confidence interval (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729), and the two-sided exact p-value. Missingness handling followed the preregistered rule 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude a pair only if both executions are unscorable); a single pair was excluded under that rule in confirmatory execution. All per-episode traces and scored artifacts required to recompute aggregations were archived.
sections.results:
Execution accounting. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed episodes correspond to 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded under the preregistered rule). Hosted-model calls used = 118 (<= planned maximum 120). Source-generation attempts = 40 (source_valid_count = 39; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1).

Primary confirmatory outcomes (complete_pairs = 39). Baseline (blind repair) success = 30/39 = 0.7692307692307693. Guarded (verifier-guided) success = 38/39 = 0.9743589743589743. Paired contingency counts (guarded, baseline): n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points). Exact two-sided paired test (McNemar exact): p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729).

Missingness. The preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule excluded one pair because its source generation was invalid/unscorable; the archived missingness_summary records both_missing_pairs = 1 and unscorable_baseline_episodes = 1 / unscorable_guarded_episodes = 1 for that index.

Representative episode diagnostics. Per-episode validator traces in the archived scoring artifacts show recurring violation codes and concrete repair behavior. Representative examples (archived scoring artifacts):
- task-000003: baseline produced a post-repair trace with violation_codes = ["PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE","UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE","FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH"] and score = 0; the guarded episode for the same shared candidate exposed validator diagnostics to the repair model and produced a post-repair trace without those violations and score = 1 (a guarded-only success contributing to n10). This episode illustrates how diagnostic exposure enabled removal or avoidance of protected-field edits flagged by the validator. 
- task-000001 and task-000002: archives show validator_trace.violation_codes and validator_feedback_exposed_to_model fields that illuminate different interaction orders and repair_call_order values across conditions; some tasks passed in both arms (n11) while others demonstrate targeted guarded corrections (contributing to n10).

Preregistered safety aggregation status. The preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation (bounding absolute increase <=5%) was not present in the archived confirmatory summary produced by the analysis executor and therefore is unresolved for confirmatory inference in this manuscript. The frozen harmful-change mapping and the per-episode validator traces required to compute that preregistered statistic were recorded during execution and permit deterministic independent recomputation; any harmful-overrepair numbers computed outside the archived confirmatory summary are exploratory.
sections.discussion:
Primary interpretation. The confirmatory paired result indicates that, for this preregistered synthetic controlled-fault bank and under shared_controlled_fault_candidate pairing semantics, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to the repair model increased the joint verifier+simulator-validated success rate from 76.92% to 97.44% (observed absolute paired increase ≈20.51 pp; exact two-sided p = 0.02148). The paired design removes variance due to source-generation differences because each pair reused the same deterministically injected controlled-fault candidate and the same initial sampled generation; differences therefore reflect the effect of exposing diagnostics given the matched repair budget and matched source generation.

Mechanism and discordant-pair structure. The discordant-pair counts (n10 = 9 vs n01 = 1) show most corrective gains occur when guarded repairs succeed on tasks where blind repair left verifier-detected violations. Archived validator_trace contents suggest two recurring mechanisms: (1) diagnostics that explicitly name protected fields (e.g., PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE) or unexpected final states (FINAL_STATE_MISMATCH) enable the model to avoid or revert edits that violate workflow constraints; and (2) diagnostics indicating omitted required steps enable the model to insert missing commands (e.g., required shut/restore sequences). The task-000003 exemplar documents an archetypal guarded correction: baseline post-repair included a protected-interface change and failed validation, while guarded repair (with validator feedback exposed) removed the offending edit and passed validation. These per-episode traces substantiate the proximate corrective mechanism without claiming generalization beyond the synthetic bank.

Difficulty, workflow patterns, and boundary behavior. Task manifests and injected_validation difficulty fields recorded per-task patterns (e.g., patterns labeled shutdown_configure_restore, make_before_break_uplink_switchover, paired_link_atomic_mtu_change) and required_command_count metadata. The archived representative tasks show that guarded corrections were especially impactful on medium/hard workflow patterns where explicit step ordering or protected-interface constraints mattered; simple single-command faults that do not trigger actionable diagnostics provide less room for improvement. The observed baseline success rate (≈77%) leaves a nontrivial headroom that permitted the observed guarded gains; in domains where baseline is already near 100% the same paired contrast would naturally shrink (a ceiling effect).

Statistical uncertainty and preregistration context. The preregistration targeted a paired design with 40 tasks and planned sensitivity to ≈30 pp effects under the original planning assumptions. The observed absolute paired difference (≈20.51 pp) produced a two-sided exact p-value = 0.02148 and a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.0769, 0.3590], demonstrating statistical detectability under the observed discordant structure (n10=9, n01=1). Complete_pairs = 39 provides reasonable precision for the observed effect size but limits power for smaller effects and for subgroup (per-fault-class) inference; all subgroup interpretations are exploratory unless recomputed on larger samples.

Safety boundary and unresolved confirmatory safety aggregation. Because the archived confirmatory analysis did not include the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation, this manuscript does not make a confirmatory safety claim about harmful over-repair. The frozen harmful-change mapping and the per-episode validator traces required to compute that aggregation were archived and allow deterministic recomputation by auditors; until such recomputation is incorporated into a confirmatory artifact, any safety aggregation remains exploratory.

Operational implications and verifier tax. Exposing diagnostics materially improved verifier-defined correctness on the tested controlled fault bank, but guarded workflows incurred additional model–verifier interactions: confirmatory execution consumed 118 hosted-model calls under the matched budget constraint (maximum 120). These counts permit exploratory computation of model-call cost per avoided failure but do not by themselves establish operational feasibility at NetOps scale; larger deployment-scale studies are required to quantify cost/latency tradeoffs, orchestration complexity, and human-in-the-loop governance implications.

Failure modes, mitigations, and future validation. Prior work documents verifier-exploitation risk when single-proxy verifiers are optimized in iterative loops [3]. Our short-horizon repair budget and shared-candidate pairing reduce exposure to long-horizon exploitation but do not eliminate it in multi-step agentic settings. Mitigations include multi-verifier ensembles, explicit harmful-change constraints (e.g., the frozen harmful-change mapping used here), calibrated abstention, and integrating uncertainty quantification. Empirical open questions include (i) harmful-overrepair rates under naturalistic task streams, (ii) multi-model robustness across vendor templates, and (iii) verifier ensembles' effectiveness at preventing exploitation while preserving correction rates.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment using a hosted validator-feedback repair adapter and shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable and substantial increase in verifier+simulator-validated configuration success (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359]). This finding is bounded to the preregistered synthetic task bank, the declared model (gpt-5-mini), and the deterministic verifier and simulator used in execution. The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test was not present in the archived confirmatory summary and therefore remains unresolved for confirmatory inference; the frozen harmful-change mapping and the per-episode validation traces recorded during execution provide exact inputs for independent reconstruction of that preregistered safety statistic. We recommend replication across multiple models and verifiers, inclusion of naturalistic task streams, and dedicated large-scale cost/latency studies to assess operational feasibility and safety at NetOps scale.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. Adapter family used for confirmatory execution: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model used for confirmatory execution: gpt-5-mini. Exact initial master prompt archived as provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10). Human role and autonomy boundary: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics: the archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset); null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The preregistered harmful-change labeling mapping used to define the planned safety aggregation was frozen before execution; the mapping and per-episode validation traces required to compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation were recorded during execution. All per-episode traces, scored artifacts, and transformation mappings needed to reproduce the preregistered secondary aggregations were recorded in the archived evidence bundle. The study followed the preregistered stopping rule.
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and counts were recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires larger-scale study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (multi-verifier designs, calibrated abstention, uncertainty quantification).

Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair test not present in archived confirmatory summary: the archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; the per-episode traces and the frozen mapping required to compute it were recorded and are available for independent reaggregation, but the preregistered confirmatory safety verdict is therefore unresolved in this paper.
